entries.result: Lemma l:2, energy of a trimmed low-energy state
entries.title: Energy bound after trimming at one cut
entries.summary: The printed proof drops two terms, one of which depends on 1/ε; the bound ε<sub>0</sub> + 6√δ and the constant chosen from it downstream have not yet been rechecked.
entries.context: Lemma l:2 trims a low-energy state to the constant Schmidt rank Bδ at one cut and bounds the energy of the result. The algorithm uses it to show that a good state of constant rank at a cut always exists, and chooses its accuracy constant cε = (ε/169)2 from this bound.
entries.claims: If δ(1 + 1/ε) ≤ 1/2 and w has energy at most ε0 + δ, the normalized trimmed state has energy at most ε0 + 6√δ.
entries.found: The proof first bounds the change in one local term by 2√δ′ with δ′ = δ(1 + 1/ε) ≥ δ, then continues with 2√δ; and of a term (1 − ε<sub>0</sub>)δ′ it keeps only −ε<sub>0</sub>δ′. Keeping both gives a bound of the form ε<sub>0</sub> + 2(δ + δ′ + 2√δ′), which depends on 1/ε. This reading comes from the tracking issue and has not yet been written up as a note.
entries.impact: Probably not. A smaller choice of cε, polynomial in ε, appears to restore the later inequality 14√cε < ε/12, which would change constants but not the polynomial running time.
entries.plan: Write the paper-gap note with the corrected bound, recheck the choice of cε and the inequality used in the proof of Lemma l:leading, and record whether only constants change.

entries.result: Theorem 1, dependence of the running time on the ground energy
entries.title: Ground energy in the exponent of the running time
entries.summary: As quoted in the tracking issue, Theorem 1 gives an exponent independent of the ground energy, but the normalization of the approximate ground-state projector contributes a factor polynomial in n only when ε0/ε is bounded; this page states the corrected exponent, and the reading has not yet been checked against the source in a note.
entries.context: The algorithm uses the operator A = ((1 − H/n)/(1 − ε0/n))m with m of order (n/ε) log n, and samples it by an average of words in the factors 1 − Hi multiplied by Cm, C = (1 − ε0/n)−1. The size of Cm controls the variance in the matrix Bernstein bound, and hence the number of sampled words.
entries.claims: Tracker #9832 quotes Theorem 1 of arXiv:1307.5143v1 (lines 213–216 of the source) as running in time nc(d, ε) poly(n/η) with c(d, ε) = 2O(log3 d/ε), with no dependence on the ground energy ε0.
entries.found: Cm = (1 − ε0/n)−m is about eε0m/n = nO(ε0/ε). The hypotheses 0 ≤ Hi ≤ 1 allow ε0 of order n, and then this factor, and with it the exponent of the running time, grows with n. Treating C2m as nO(1/ε) requires ε0 bounded. The corrected exponent is 2O(log3 d/ε) + O(ε0/ε).
entries.impact: The algorithm is polynomial-time whenever ε<sub>0</sub>/ε is bounded, in particular for frustration-free chains; for an extensive ground energy the stated bound does not give polynomial time. The formalization targets existence statements, not running times, so no formal statement depends on this.
entries.plan: Check the printed statement and the sampling estimate against the source, write the paper-gap note, and correct the result table in #9832.
